misconceptions.believed: There is always a step after the edit point, so stepping once after an edit takes the count from 2 to 3.
misconceptions.revealed_by: AssertionError: 2 != 3. The fixed source ends on the line the fast-forward stops at, so the next step ends the run and appends nothing.
misconceptions.corrected_to: How many events exist after a point is a property of the code being run, not of the engine. The test now uses a source with a line after the edit point, plus a separate assertion that the fast-forward leaves the child blocked rather than finished, which is the property actually meant.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: M33's family again: the code was right and the test was wrong, and the reflex on a failing assertion is to suspect the code.

misconceptions.believed: A live boss step returning True had passed. _live_step returns a bool and the CLI prints BOSS DOWN on three of them, so a live fight was being checked.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Reading _run_stepped while wiring --fix. It calls fn(*args) and discards the value; step mode filled no outcomes, and _live_step's only test was 'if result.error'. A live fight was cleared by not raising.
misconceptions.corrected_to: Step mode reports one outcome for the test it runs, and the CLI checks it. A step cleared by 'return None' is now caught. Scoring the fight is still W6/W7; this is only the difference between not crashing and answering.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: M1's shape: a thing that looked measured and was not. Without it, exit criterion 3 - editing the paused line and resuming completes the fight - would have been satisfiable by an edit that answers nothing, and the evidence written for it would have been false. Both were only visible from asking what a lazy solution would do.

decisions.decision: Edit-and-resume is strategy A: re-run from the top and fast-forward to the edit point
decisions.rationale: The memo A needs is the test payload the parent already holds, so replay costs nothing and cannot drift. T3 recommended A and asked that we measure how often it is wrong.

decisions.decision: W5 lands with W4 rather than after it
alternatives: Ship the resume now, add the detector next session
decisions.rationale: Strategy A is a claim about the part the player did not watch again. Shipping the claim without the check is shipping the thing exit criterion 4 forbids.

decisions.decision: The fast-forward stops at the edit point, never through it
alternatives: Replay through it and compare the whole prefix
decisions.rationale: The edited step is the one that is supposed to differ. Replaying it undoes the edit and makes divergence fire on every successful fix.

decisions.decision: The edit point is the cursor, not the end of history
alternatives: Always resume from where the child is blocked
decisions.rationale: The player edits the line they are looking at, and W3 already tracks that.

decisions.decision: A step's signature excludes the line number
decisions.rationale: The player just moved the text, and moved text is not different behaviour. A detector that fires on every edit gets ignored. Accepts a false negative on adjacent statements with identical locals.

decisions.decision: edit returns the divergence; the caller decides how loudly to report it
decisions.rationale: Only the caller knows who is watching, and runner.py must not grow display opinions.

decisions.decision: A divergent resume continues the fight with a warning
decisions.rationale: It is still playable, it is just not continuous. Criterion 4 asks that the player be told, not that the run be stopped.

decisions.decision: Step mode reports one outcome for the test it runs
alternatives: Leave correctness to W6 and W7
decisions.rationale: Without it, 'the fight completes' means 'nothing raised', and this session's evidence for criterion 3 would be false. Not scoring; the signal scoring will be built on.

friction.description: close() was not re-entrant across a restart: it sets _closed and returns early, which an edit needs to undo. Split into close (and never again) and _teardown (shut the child down).
An f-string with implicit string concatenation inside the expression is a syntax error before 3.12, and this machine is pinned to 3.11 (M5). Caught by the import.
Choosing what counts as divergence took longer than implementing it. The right ratio for this waypoint, and it produced no wasted artefact.

handoff.state: T3 W4 and W5 are landed together. LiveRun.edit re-runs edited source and fast-forwards to the edit point; timeline.compare says when the fast-forward stopped matching, and the fast-forward stops there. Step mode now reports whether the step answered. T3 exit criteria 1, 2, 3 and 4 are verified; 5 and 6 remain. 887 tests green unpinned, verify clean on 45 reference runs.
handoff.next_action: T3 W6, the boss HP model tied to first-try step completions. D132 put the signal in place, so HP has something honest to consume. Read M35 first: that signal exists because its absence would have made a criterion claimable by a fix that answers nothing, and HP is the next thing that could be gamed the same way. Before W6, decide Q67: --fix proves the engine but is a file path rather than a keystroke, and criterion 6 is held open on it. Scoring an experience nobody can drive by hand is the wrong order.

open_questions.question: Nothing lets a player type an edit into a paused fight: --fix is a file path. Does the edit belong in boss --live as a keystroke, in the T7 editor, or somewhere else? Criterion 6 is held open on it.
Two events land on one line when it raises. Should the display merge them into one entry carrying both the values and the failure?
Timeline holds Step objects for a live run and dicts for a recorded one. compare now handles both by inspection, which works and is a second place that knows about two shapes.
The recording cap is 400 steps, so an edit made past step 400 of a longer run fast-forwards against a truncated original. Divergence would be reported against history the engine does not have.
T3's instrument check - divergence rate over real play, with ~5% justifying strategy C - is measurable and uncollected. Where would the counter live, given that runs are not persisted?

A stepped run executes tests[0] only, so a live boss step is cleared on one case while the same step scored normally faces all of them. Is one case enough to call a step passed, once W6 ties HP to it?
